title: What does LoanPay do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LoanPay and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LoanPay makes a repayment against an active loan under its configured terms. [1]

The loan's schedule, asset and payment rules determine how the amount affects outstanding obligations. An ordinary transfer to a broker is not automatically equivalent to this loan-specific operation. Check the resulting balance and status in validated metadata. Repayment evidence supports the named loan only and should not be generalized to the broker's entire credit portfolio. [1]

The LoanPay reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LoanPay, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
